description.p: ZQuest Classic is an engine for making and playing top-down adventure games in the style of 80s and 90s classics. It started as a dungeon crawler engine and has grown into a modern one, with most of its features available without any programming.

The included player runs quests made by the community, and the editor lets you build your own, with maps, dungeons, enemies, items and music. For more advanced games, the ZScript language adds full scripting support.
Open the launcher to choose the player or the editor, or open a quest file to start playing it right away.

A security update that hardens the script engine and the loading of damaged or malicious quests, saves and music files, along with many crash fixes. Also adds the "Once Per Weapon" combo trigger effect.

A big controller update: hundreds more controllers work out of the box, and each gets its own control scheme with sensible defaults and a simpler binding screen. Also adds a quest browser on editor startup, more portable save files, and a choice to quit or reload the last save in standalone mode. Older quests load faster and idle CPU usage is much lower. Fixed replay uploading running for users who had not opted in.

Enhanced music can be found in a subfolder next to the quest, and dropdowns open when clicked anywhere. Fixed console music (NSF, SPC, etc.) playing at half volume and MIDIs sounding detuned, and sped up levels with palette cycling.

Stomp Boots item wizard, tile editor improvements, more invincibility and knockback options, and the subscreen editor outlines otherwise-invisible widgets. Dark rooms and fades are faster, and a crash on older CPUs is fixed.

Better name entry, improved quest auto-backups and timed auto-saves, a "DMap Levels" quest report, and a search bar in some older list dialogs. Fixed sprites drawing over the subscreen in many older quests.
Save files with long replays load much faster, single replays can be uploaded manually, and a scripts folder next to the quest is automatically an include path.
Multiple control schemes in the player. The editor's map view can zoom and drag with the mouse, and tile drawing is faster. Fixed sound on many Linux distros.
A "Script Bugfix" option for new quests, and Trace accepts strings.

A large batch of fixes (lifting, conveyors, the bottom 8 pixels, saving in test mode) and Cambria tileset updates. ZScript gained a writable Screen->Flag[] and a quest rule to run weapon scripts during spawn.

The bottom 8 pixels of the screen are now visible, with a quest rule and a player setting to control it. The tile editor gained Reference Tiles. ZScript gained Screen->DrawOrigin, more range types, _ digit separators, and several additions for 3.0 compatibility. The classic NES quests are no longer bundled.
"Only Grounded Weapons" trigger flag, a "full" color for subscreen counters, the Cambria tileset, and a -smart-assign command line switch to compile and assign scripts.
An Auto-Save option for test mode (no more unsaved-changes prompt), the editor explains why a quest failed to load, and new Dense Forest and Extension autocombo modes.
Tracker music (mod, it, s3m, xm) supports loop points, and scripts can control its position and speed. Text fields gained Ctrl+Backspace / Alt+Backspace to delete a word or line.
Opt-in automatic uploading of replays, to help the developers catch bugs.
Note item wizard, an enemy flag to opt out of "Kill All Enemies", and an option to use the native OS file dialog. Fixed scripts on large enemies stopping after one frame, and reduced CPU usage.
Scripts compile much faster with the JIT, and very large scripts can now be compiled too. Fixed the editor's "Used Tiles" calculation.
Per-screen editor notes, and the FFC editor previews large FFCs.
The Deep is included in the release package. Fixed generic script InitD[] not working, and a few crashes.

The first stable 2.55 release, and the biggest update since 2.50: full Linux and Mac support, a reworked editor with test mode and a new subscreen editor, unlimited save files with replays, generic scripts and a Visual Studio Code extension, and many new item and combo types, real dark rooms, pitfalls and light beam puzzles.
